holidays.name: National Superhero Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating caped crusaders, masked vigilantes, and everyday heroes. Fans dress up as their favorite heroes, binge-watch comic book movies, and dig out dusty comic collections.
holidays.origin: Popularized as an unofficial US observance in the early 2000s, reportedly started by a Marvel Comics fan and promoted through comic and pop culture circles. It has no official government recognition.
holidays.funFact: Superman debuted in Action Comics #1 in 1938, and a copy of that issue sold for millions of dollars at auction, making it one of the most valuable comic books ever.

holidays.name: National Great Poetry Reading Day
holidays.description: A day to read poems out loud, whether in a cafe, in your living room, or to your very confused cat. It encourages people to step away from screens and let rhythm and rhyme take over.
holidays.origin: Poetry-reading celebrations have been informally observed on or around this date in the US, promoted by literary groups and poetry lovers, though the exact origin is murky.
holidays.funFact: Many of the oldest known poems were composed to be spoken or sung aloud, long before they were ever written down.

holidays.name: Workers' Memorial Day (International Workers' Memorial Day)
holidays.description: A solemn but important observance honoring workers who have been killed, injured, or made ill by their jobs. Candlelight vigils and moments of silence are common.
holidays.origin: Started by the labor movement in Canada in 1984 and later adopted by the AFL-CIO and international trade unions. April 28 was chosen partly because the US Occupational Safety and Health Act took effect on this date in 1971.
holidays.funFact: The International Labour Organization also marks April 28 as the World Day for Safety and Health at Work, so the day carries both a memorial and a prevention message worldwide.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in a slice of the deep purple dessert, ideally with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top. Be prepared for blue teeth and zero regrets.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that is observed in the US by bakers, food bloggers, and pie fans. Its exact creator is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America, and they were eaten by Indigenous peoples long before pie recipes existed.

holidays.name: Great Poetry Reading Day Sidekick: Kiss Your Mate Day
holidays.description: A sweet and slightly awkward occasion encouraging couples to share a kiss, no excuses needed. It works well for forgetful partners as a last-minute romantic gesture.
holidays.origin: Kiss Your Mate Day is an informal, lighthearted observance listed in quirky holiday calendars, with no clear founder or documented first celebration.
holidays.funFact: Scientists who study kissing, known as philematologists, say a kiss can quickly boost feel-good chemicals like oxytocin and dopamine in the brain.
